This report audits missing values in the canonical analysis-entry file
`Res_2_Data_for_Analysis/dat_focal_analysis.rda`. Baseline variables are first
checked at the participant level. Because the selected baseline demographics
and psychological items contain no missing values, the substantive missing-
value analysis focuses on prompt-level EMA data.

The corresponding Excel result is
`Res_3_Results/Table_S1_5_MVA_Report.xlsx`. No CSV output is created.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  collapse = FALSE,
  comment = NA
)

required_packages <- c("dplyr", "knitr", "openxlsx", "psych", "rmarkdown", "tidyr", "xml2", "zip")
package_available <- vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (!all(package_available)) {
  stop("Missing required R packages: ", paste(names(package_available)[!package_available], collapse = ", "))
}

locate_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  if (!dir.exists(candidate)) candidate <- dirname(candidate)
  repeat {
    if (all(dir.exists(file.path(candidate, c(
      "Step_1_Descriptive_and_Reliability", "Step_2_Measurement_Models"
    ))))) return(candidate)
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) break
    candidate <- parent
  }
  stop("Could not identify the project root from the public Step folders")
}

input_context <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
project_root <- locate_project_root(
  if (length(input_context) == 1L && !is.na(input_context) && nzchar(input_context)) {
    input_context
  } else getwd()
)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

input_file <- file.path(project_root, "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis", "dat_focal_analysis.rda")
excel_output <- file.path(project_root, "Res_3_Results", "Table_S1_5_MVA_Report.xlsx")
if (!file.exists(input_file)) stop("Missing canonical analysis-entry RDA: ", input_file)
```

# Helper functions

```{r helpers}
correlation_display <- function(r, p) {
  stars <- ifelse(p < .001, "***", ifelse(p < .01, "**", ifelse(p <= .05, "*", "")))
  matrix(sprintf("%.3f%s", r, stars), nrow = nrow(r), dimnames = dimnames(r))
}

cross_correlation <- function(data, x_variables, y_variables, x_labels, y_labels) {
  x <- data[x_variables]
  y <- data[y_variables]
  names(x) <- unname(x_labels[x_variables])
  names(y) <- unname(y_labels[y_variables])

  result <- psych::corr.test(
    x,
    y,
    use = "complete",
    method = "pearson",
    adjust = "none",
    ci = FALSE
  )

  list(
    r = result$r,
    p = result$p,
    n = min(result$n),
    display = correlation_display(result$r, result$p)
  )
}

correlation_long <- function(result, analysis) {
  indices <- expand.grid(
    missingness_variable = rownames(result$r),
    outcome = colnames(result$r),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  indices$r <- as.vector(result$r)
  indices$p <- as.vector(result$p)
  indices$stars <- ifelse(
    indices$p < .001, "***",
    ifelse(indices$p < .01, "**", ifelse(indices$p <= .05, "*", ""))
  )
  indices$analysis <- analysis
  indices$n <- result$n
  indices[, c("analysis", "missingness_variable", "outcome", "n", "r", "p", "stars")]
}

descriptive_summary <- function(data, variables, labels) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(variables, function(variable) {
    x <- data[[variable]]
    data.frame(
      variable = variable,
      label = unname(labels[[variable]]),
      n = length(x),
      mean = mean(x),
      sd = stats::sd(x),
      median = stats::median(x),
      q1 = unname(stats::quantile(x, .25)),
      q3 = unname(stats::quantile(x, .75)),
      minimum = min(x),
      maximum = max(x),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}
```

# Baseline missing-value audit

The audit covers the eight sample-description variables and all four baseline
psychological item sets. Baseline fields are first verified to be constant
within each participant and then reduced to one row per `Name_ID`.

```{r baseline-audit}
baseline_demographic_vars <- c(
  "AgeInYears", "Gender", "Grade", "FamilyResidence",
  "ParentsMaritalStatus", "ParentsHighestEdu",
  "TotalFamilyIncome", "SiblingStructure"
)
baseline_item_vars <- c(
  paste0("V_BSMAS_", 1:18),
  paste0("K_CESD_", 1:7),
  paste0("L_DASS_", 1:7),
  paste0("M_PSS_", 1:10)
)
baseline_audit_vars <- c(baseline_demographic_vars, baseline_item_vars)

baseline_constancy <- vapply(
  baseline_audit_vars,
  function(variable) {
    max(vapply(
      split(dat_focal_analysis[[variable]], dat_focal_analysis$Name_ID),
      function(x) dplyr::n_distinct(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      integer(1)
    ))
  },
  integer(1)
)
if (any(baseline_constancy > 1L)) {
  stop("Baseline fields vary within person: ", paste(names(baseline_constancy)[baseline_constancy > 1L], collapse = ", "))
}

dat_baseline <- dat_focal_analysis |>
  dplyr::distinct(Name_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(Name_ID, dplyr::all_of(baseline_audit_vars)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID)

baseline_missing_by_variable <- data.frame(
  variable = baseline_audit_vars,
  missing_n = vapply(dat_baseline[baseline_audit_vars], function(x) sum(is.na(x)), integer(1)),
  missing_proportion = vapply(dat_baseline[baseline_audit_vars], function(x) mean(is.na(x)), numeric(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

baseline_audit_summary <- data.frame(
  participants = nrow(dat_baseline),
  variables_audited = length(baseline_audit_vars),
  missing_cells = sum(baseline_missing_by_variable$missing_n),
  participants_with_any_missing = sum(!stats::complete.cases(dat_baseline)),
  conclusion = if (sum(baseline_missing_by_variable$missing_n) == 0L) {
    "No missing baseline values; subsequent MVA focuses on EMA."
  } else {
    "Baseline missing values detected; inspect variable-level audit."
  },
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

baseline_audit_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline audit",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
stopifnot(sum(baseline_missing_by_variable$missing_n) == 0L)
```

# EMA missingness

## Source-variable missing proportions

```{r ema-source-missingness}
ema_source_vars <- c(
  paste0("PMU", 1:6),
  paste0("DASS", 1:6),
  paste0("mu_time", 1:3),
  paste0("mu_frequency", 1:3)
)

ema_source_labels <- c(
  setNames(paste("Momentary PSMU item", 1:6), paste0("PMU", 1:6)),
  setNames(paste("Momentary distress item", 1:6), paste0("DASS", 1:6)),
  mu_time1 = "Messaging time", mu_time2 = "Posting time", mu_time3 = "Browsing time",
  mu_frequency1 = "Messaging frequency", mu_frequency2 = "Posting frequency",
  mu_frequency3 = "Browsing frequency"
)

ema_source_missingness <- data.frame(
  variable = ema_source_vars,
  label = unname(ema_source_labels[ema_source_vars]),
  prompt_rows = nrow(dat_focal_analysis),
  observed_n = vapply(dat_focal_analysis[ema_source_vars], function(x) sum(!is.na(x)), integer(1)),
  missing_n = vapply(dat_focal_analysis[ema_source_vars], function(x) sum(is.na(x)), integer(1)),
  missing_proportion = vapply(dat_focal_analysis[ema_source_vars], function(x) mean(is.na(x)), numeric(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

ema_source_missingness |>
  dplyr::mutate(missing_proportion = round(missing_proportion, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Ema source missingness",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Focal-measure missing proportions

A prompt-level focal measure is considered observed only when every item needed
for that measure is observed. The six engagement variables remain single-item
measures. Person means below use all available complete prompts for that
specific focal measure; no participant has an entirely missing focal measure.

```{r ema-focal-missingness}
ema_measure_items <- list(
  Momentary_PSMU = paste0("PMU", 1:6),
  Momentary_Stress = paste0("DASS", 1:2),
  Momentary_Anxiety = paste0("DASS", 3:4),
  Momentary_Depression = paste0("DASS", 5:6),
  Messaging_Time = "mu_time1",
  Posting_Time = "mu_time2",
  Browsing_Time = "mu_time3",
  Messaging_Frequency = "mu_frequency1",
  Posting_Frequency = "mu_frequency2",
  Browsing_Frequency = "mu_frequency3"
)
ema_measure_labels <- c(
  Momentary_PSMU = "Momentary PSMU",
  Momentary_Stress = "Momentary stress",
  Momentary_Anxiety = "Momentary anxiety",
  Momentary_Depression = "Momentary depression",
  Messaging_Time = "Messaging time",
  Posting_Time = "Posting time",
  Browsing_Time = "Browsing time",
  Messaging_Frequency = "Messaging frequency",
  Posting_Frequency = "Posting frequency",
  Browsing_Frequency = "Browsing frequency"
)

ema_scored <- dat_focal_analysis
for (measure in names(ema_measure_items)) {
  items <- ema_measure_items[[measure]]
  complete <- stats::complete.cases(ema_scored[items])
  ema_scored[[paste0("Complete_", measure)]] <- complete
  ema_scored[[paste0("Score_", measure)]] <- ifelse(
    complete,
    rowMeans(ema_scored[items]),
    NA_real_
  )
}

ema_measure_missingness <- data.frame(
  measure = names(ema_measure_items),
  label = unname(ema_measure_labels[names(ema_measure_items)]),
  required_items = vapply(ema_measure_items, length, integer(1)),
  prompt_rows = nrow(ema_scored),
  observed_n = vapply(
    names(ema_measure_items),
    function(x) sum(ema_scored[[paste0("Complete_", x)]]),
    integer(1)
  ),
  missing_n = vapply(
    names(ema_measure_items),
    function(x) sum(!ema_scored[[paste0("Complete_", x)]]),
    integer(1)
  ),
  missing_proportion = vapply(
    names(ema_measure_items),
    function(x) mean(!ema_scored[[paste0("Complete_", x)]]),
    numeric(1)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

ema_measure_missingness |>
  dplyr::mutate(missing_proportion = round(missing_proportion, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Ema focal missingness",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

# EMA response compliance

The canonical data contain all 90 scheduled prompt rows per participant. Two
compliance definitions are reported:

- any-response compliance: at least one of the 18 EMA source variables was
  observed at the scheduled prompt;
- complete-focal compliance: all 18 EMA source variables were observed.

```{r ema-compliance}
ema_scored <- ema_scored |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Any_Response = rowSums(!is.na(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(ema_source_vars)))) > 0,
    Complete_Focal_Response = stats::complete.cases(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(ema_source_vars)))
  )

person_compliance <- ema_scored |>
  dplyr::group_by(Name_ID) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    scheduled_days = dplyr::n_distinct(Day),
    expected_prompts = dplyr::n(),
    any_response_n = sum(Any_Response),
    any_response_compliance = mean(Any_Response),
    complete_focal_n = sum(Complete_Focal_Response),
    complete_focal_compliance = mean(Complete_Focal_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID)

stopifnot(
  all(person_compliance$scheduled_days == 30L),
  all(person_compliance$expected_prompts == 90L)
)

complete_focal_prompt_total <- sum(ema_scored$Complete_Focal_Response)
overall_complete_focal_compliance <- mean(ema_scored$Complete_Focal_Response)
person_complete_focal_mean <- mean(person_compliance$complete_focal_compliance)
person_complete_focal_sd <- stats::sd(person_compliance$complete_focal_compliance)
person_complete_focal_min <- min(person_compliance$complete_focal_compliance)
person_complete_focal_max <- max(person_compliance$complete_focal_compliance)

compliance_labels <- c(
  any_response_n = "Any-response prompts",
  any_response_compliance = "Any-response compliance",
  complete_focal_n = "Complete-focal prompts",
  complete_focal_compliance = "Complete-focal compliance"
)
compliance_summary <- descriptive_summary(
  person_compliance,
  names(compliance_labels),
  compliance_labels
)

compliance_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Ema compliance",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

Across all `r format(nrow(ema_scored), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`
scheduled EMA prompts,
`r format(complete_focal_prompt_total, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`
prompts contained complete data on all EMA focal variables, corresponding to
an overall compliance rate of
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * overall_complete_focal_compliance)`. At the person
level, the mean complete-focal compliance rate was
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * person_complete_focal_mean)`
(SD = `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * person_complete_focal_sd)`). Individual
person-level compliance rates ranged from
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * person_complete_focal_min)` to
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * person_complete_focal_max)`.

# Person-level missingness associations

## Construct person-level missingness and focal means

```{r person-level-data}
person_measure_data <- ema_scored |>
  dplyr::group_by(Name_ID) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::starts_with("Complete_"),
      ~ mean(!.x),
      .names = "Missing_{sub('Complete_', '', .col)}"
    ),
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::starts_with("Score_"),
      ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      .names = "Mean_{sub('Score_', '', .col)}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

missing_rate_vars <- paste0("Missing_", names(ema_measure_items))
person_mean_vars <- paste0("Mean_", names(ema_measure_items))

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(person_measure_data[missing_rate_vars]),
  !anyNA(person_measure_data[person_mean_vars]),
  all(vapply(person_measure_data[missing_rate_vars], stats::sd, numeric(1)) > 0)
)

missing_rate_labels <- setNames(
  paste("Missing rate:", unname(ema_measure_labels[names(ema_measure_items)])),
  missing_rate_vars
)
person_mean_labels <- setNames(
  paste("Person mean:", unname(ema_measure_labels[names(ema_measure_items)])),
  person_mean_vars
)
```

## Baseline outcomes

Baseline scale totals use the same scoring as S1.4: baseline anxiety items are
shifted from 1-4 to 0-3 using `x - 1`, and `M_PSS_4`, `M_PSS_5`, `M_PSS_7`,
and `M_PSS_8` are reverse-scored using `6 - x`. Gender is coded female = 1,
male = 0.

```{r baseline-outcomes}
pss_items <- paste0("M_PSS_", 1:10)
pss_reverse_items <- paste0("M_PSS_", c(4, 5, 7, 8))
baseline_scored <- dat_baseline
baseline_scored[pss_reverse_items] <- lapply(
  baseline_scored[pss_reverse_items],
  function(x) 6 - x
)

baseline_scored <- baseline_scored |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Trait_PSMU_Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(paste0("V_BSMAS_", 1:18)))),
    Depression_Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(paste0("K_CESD_", 1:7)))),
    Anxiety_Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(paste0("L_DASS_", 1:7)), ~ .x - 1)),
    Perceived_Stress_Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(pss_items))),
    Gender_Female = dplyr::case_when(
      as.character(Gender) == "F" ~ 1,
      as.character(Gender) == "M" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

baseline_outcome_vars <- c(
  "Trait_PSMU_Total", "Depression_Total", "Anxiety_Total",
  "Perceived_Stress_Total", "AgeInYears", "Gender_Female"
)
baseline_outcome_labels <- c(
  Trait_PSMU_Total = "Baseline trait PSMU",
  Depression_Total = "Baseline depression",
  Anxiety_Total = "Baseline anxiety",
  Perceived_Stress_Total = "Baseline perceived stress",
  AgeInYears = "Age",
  Gender_Female = "Gender (female=1)"
)

person_mva_data <- person_measure_data |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    baseline_scored |>
      dplyr::select(Name_ID, dplyr::all_of(baseline_outcome_vars)),
    by = "Name_ID"
  )

stopifnot(nrow(person_mva_data) == 209L, !anyNA(person_mva_data))
```

## Correlations with EMA focal person means

All person-level correlations are Pearson correlations with two-sided,
unadjusted p values. Results use no star for `p > .05`, `*` for
`.01 <= p <= .05`, `**` for `.001 <= p < .01`, and `***` for `p < .001`.

```{r missingness-ema-correlations}
missingness_ema_correlation <- cross_correlation(
  person_mva_data,
  missing_rate_vars,
  person_mean_vars,
  missing_rate_labels,
  person_mean_labels
)

missingness_ema_correlation$display |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Missingness ema correlations",
    row.names = TRUE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Significant associations summary

The following table summarizes the exploratory associations. Because multiple tests are performed, the unadjusted p values should be interpreted as diagnostics of
possible selective missingness rather than definitive hypothesis tests.

```{r significant-associations}
missingness_correlation_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  correlation_long(missingness_ema_correlation, "EMA missing rate vs EMA person mean"),
  correlation_long(missingness_baseline_correlation, "EMA missing rate vs baseline/demographic")
)

significant_missingness_associations <- missingness_correlation_long |>
  dplyr::filter(p <= .05) |>
  dplyr::arrange(analysis, p, missingness_variable, outcome)

data.frame(
  total_tests = nrow(missingness_correlation_long),
  significant_at_05_unadjusted = nrow(significant_missingness_associations),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Significant associations",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )

significant_missingness_associations |>
  dplyr::mutate(r = round(r, 3), p = signif(p, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Significant associations (2)",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

# Excel results

`Res_3_Results/Table_S1_5_MVA_Report.xlsx` contains `Missingness`, `Compliance`,
and `Correlations`. The compliance sheet includes participant-level records
and must remain with the private results, not in the public repository.
Correlation displays retain their unadjusted significance stars; numerical
summaries retain full available precision. `write_artifacts: false` disables
only file writes, not the analyses earlier in this report.

```{r export-excel}
if (isTRUE(params$write_artifacts)) {
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook(creator = "Kunru Song")
  header_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", wrapText = TRUE)
  decimal_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "0.0000")
  integer_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "0")

  normalize_openxml_relationships <- function(path) {
    # Remove only worksheet drawing/VML relationships whose internal targets
    # are absent. Preserve valid drawings, external links and all other parts.
    unpack_dir <- tempfile("s1_5_xlsx_")
    dir.create(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    on.exit(unlink(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE), add = TRUE)

    members <- utils::unzip(path, list = TRUE)$Name
    unsafe_member <- function(member) {
      parts <- strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "/", member), "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
      grepl("^[/\\\\]|^[A-Za-z]:", member) || any(parts == "..")
    }
    stopifnot(length(members) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(members),
              !any(vapply(members, unsafe_member, logical(1))))
    utils::unzip(path, exdir = unpack_dir)
    relationship_files <- list.files(
      file.path(unpack_dir, "xl", "worksheets", "_rels"),
      pattern = "[.]rels$", full.names = TRUE
    )
    if (!length(relationship_files)) return(invisible(path))

    resolve_member <- function(target) {
      target <- gsub("\\\\", "/", utils::URLdecode(target))
      if (!nzchar(target) || grepl("^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:", target)) {
        stop("Invalid internal drawing target")
      }
      parts <- strsplit(target, "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
      result <- if (startsWith(target, "/")) character() else c("xl", "worksheets")
      for (part in parts) {
        if (!nzchar(part) || part == ".") next
        if (part == "..") {
          if (!length(result)) stop("Drawing target escapes the workbook package")
          result <- head(result, -1L)
        } else result <- c(result, part)
      }
      paste(result, collapse = "/")
    }
    drawing_types <- paste0(
      "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/",
      c("drawing", "vmlDrawing")
    )
    removed_relationships <- 0L
    for (relationship_file in relationship_files) {
      document <- xml2::read_xml(relationship_file, options = "NONET")
      relationships <- xml2::xml_find_all(
        document, "/*[local-name()='Relationships']/*[local-name()='Relationship']"
      )
      changed <- FALSE
      for (relationship in relationships) {
        type <- xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "Type")
        external <- identical(xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "TargetMode"), "External")
        if (!type %in% drawing_types || external) next
        target <- xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "Target")
        if (is.na(target)) stop("Drawing relationship is missing its Target")
        if (!resolve_member(target) %in% members) {
          xml2::xml_remove(relationship)
          removed_relationships <- removed_relationships + 1L
          changed <- TRUE
        }
      }
      if (changed) xml2::write_xml(document, relationship_file)
    }
    if (removed_relationships == 0L) return(invisible(path))

    normalized_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
    on.exit(unlink(normalized_file, force = TRUE), add = TRUE)
    zip::zipr(
      normalized_file,
      files = list.files(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE),
      root = unpack_dir,
      include_directories = FALSE,
      mode = "mirror"
    )
    if (!file.copy(normalized_file, path, overwrite = TRUE)) {
      stop("Could not replace the workbook with its normalized OpenXML package.")
    }
    unlink(normalized_file, force = TRUE)
    invisible(path)
  }

  write_result_section <- function(sheet, title, data, headers, start_row,
                                   integer_columns = integer()) {
    stopifnot(is.data.frame(data), ncol(data) == length(headers))
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet, title, startRow = start_row, colNames = FALSE)
    names(data) <- headers
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet, data, startRow = start_row + 1L,
                        rowNames = FALSE, headerStyle = header_style, keepNA = TRUE)
    if (nrow(data)) {
      rows <- seq.int(start_row + 2L, length.out = nrow(data))
      numeric_columns <- which(vapply(data, is.numeric, logical(1)))
      for (column in numeric_columns) {
        openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sheet,
          if (column %in% integer_columns) integer_style else decimal_style,
          rows = rows, cols = column, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE)
      }
    }
    start_row + nrow(data) + 4L
  }

  for (sheet in c("Missingness", "Compliance", "Correlations")) {
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet, gridLines = FALSE)
    openxlsx::freezePane(wb, sheet, firstActiveRow = 3L)
  }
  next_row <- write_result_section("Missingness", "Baseline missingness",
    baseline_audit_summary,
    c("Participants", "Variables audited", "Missing cells",
      "Participants with any missing", "Conclusion"), 1L, 1:4)
  next_row <- write_result_section("Missingness", "EMA source-variable missingness",
    ema_source_missingness,
    c("Variable", "Label", "Prompt rows", "Observed N", "Missing N", "Missing proportion"),
    next_row, 3:5)
  write_result_section("Missingness", "EMA focal-measure missingness",
    ema_measure_missingness,
    c("Measure", "Label", "Required items", "Prompt rows", "Observed N", "Missing N",
      "Missing proportion"), next_row, 3:6)

  next_row <- write_result_section("Compliance", "Participant compliance summary",
    compliance_summary,
    c("Variable", "Label", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Median", "Q1", "Q3", "Minimum", "Maximum"),
    1L, 3L)
  compliance_detail <- dplyr::left_join(
    person_compliance[c("Name_ID", "scheduled_days", "expected_prompts", "any_response_n",
      "any_response_compliance", "complete_focal_n", "complete_focal_compliance")],
    person_measure_data[c("Name_ID", missing_rate_vars)], by = "Name_ID")
  write_result_section("Compliance", "Participant compliance and missing proportions",
    compliance_detail, names(compliance_detail), next_row, c(1:4, 6L))

  next_row <- write_result_section("Correlations", "Exploratory unadjusted tests",
    data.frame(total_tests = nrow(missingness_correlation_long),
      significant_at_05_unadjusted = nrow(significant_missingness_associations)),
    c("Total tests", "Significant at p <= .05 (unadjusted)"), 1L, 1:2)
  for (result in list(missingness_ema_correlation, missingness_baseline_correlation)) {
    display_table <- data.frame(Variable = rownames(result$display),
      result$display, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
    next_row <- write_result_section("Correlations",
      if (identical(colnames(result$display), colnames(missingness_ema_correlation$display))) {
        "Missing proportions versus EMA focal person means"
      } else "Missing proportions versus baseline totals, age and gender",
      display_table, names(display_table), next_row)
  }
  write_result_section("Correlations", "Associations significant at unadjusted p <= .05",
    significant_missingness_associations,
    c("Analysis", "Missingness variable", "Outcome", "N", "r", "p", "Stars"), next_row, 4L)
  for (sheet in c("Missingness", "Compliance", "Correlations")) {
    openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sheet, cols = 1:17, widths = 24)
    openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sheet, cols = 1:2, widths = 42)
  }
  dir.create(dirname(excel_output), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, excel_output, overwrite = TRUE)
  normalize_openxml_relationships(excel_output)
}
```
